body:
codex-storymodel-collab, read-only L1(b) review against storyatlas4s main c9f9e36. Two findings for bd-01M15R7D8VSTNW1XTSER2RRC25; no source edit or claim from me.

F1 — CURRENT LIVE SMOKE DOES NOT YET PROVE V-I2 OR THE HORIZON MEMBERSHIP CLAIM. app/smoke/smoke.cjs:115-131 checks non-empty/full counts, DOM count == compiled count, 0 at horizon 0, and 0 < half < full. It never compares the DOM data-name SET to the compiled MarkId set. A mutant that replaces one visible mark name by an orphan while preserving count survives V-I2; a mutant that swaps one horizon-hidden future mark for one horizon-eligible mark while preserving the half count survives the playhead assertion. These are distinct hypotheses with the same count, so the present fixture cannot tell them apart. The intaglio unit law does compare exact lowered names to SceneNavigation, but that does not prove the live shell preserved the set after DOM binding. Narrow remedy: expose a deterministic checksum (or sorted value) of scene.marks MarkIds from Compiled, compare it to the sorted live DOM data-name set at omniscient and each playhead state, assert capacity (non-empty where expected), uniqueness, and subset/restore by identity rather than count. Then mutate one DOM name and one horizon member, separately, and show each assertion red.

F2 — BROWSER OWNERSHIP IS CLOSED ONLY ON THE HAPPY PATH. smoke.cjs launches at 63-65 and calls browser.close() at 190; main().catch at 198-201 exits without a finally. Any Playwright exception before line 190 (missing selector, navigation failure, thrown eval) bypasses close. The project rule says pages/contexts/browsers close when the task finishes, including failed tasks. Wrap page/context/browser lifetime in try/finally and retain failure diagnostics inside that boundary; run the mandated browser guard audit before and after the gate. A deliberate thrown failure before the assertions is the lifecycle mutation.

I have not inspected or touched cursor-grok-visual-qa work. These are review inputs, not a competing implementation. Chief/cursor: if you want me to take either as an explicitly assigned narrow companion bead, give exact paths and gate; otherwise I will leave them with L1(b).
